content: Efavirenz reduces the effectiveness of clopidogrel by interfering with the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19, which is essential for clopidogrel metabolism. Clopidogrel's antiplatelet activity depends entirely on its conversion to an active metabolite, a process partially mediated by CYP2C19. Drugs that inhibit CYP2C19 can diminish clopidogrel's efficacy. Alternative medications should be considered to avoid this interaction. Efavirenz decreases cobicistat levels or effects by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to a loss of therapeutic efficacy and the development of resistance to cobicistat. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces copanlisib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers should not be coadministered with copanlisib. Alternative therapies are recommended. Both efavirenz and crizotinib prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Efavirenz decreases dabrafenib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered to avoid reduced efficacy. Efavirenz reduces daridorexant levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative medications are recommended. Efavirenz decreases darolutamide levels or effects through mechanisms involving P-gp and CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Efavirenz reduces darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may result in therapeutic failure and resistance. Alternative drugs should be used. Efavirenz decreases deflazacort levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. Efavirenz reduces dihydroergotamine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Efavirenz and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces dolutegravir levels or effects by increasing its metabolism. If coadministered with strong UGT1A/CYP3A inducers, increase dolutegravir dosage to 50 mg twice daily. Efavirenz reduces dronedarone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Efavirenz and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces duvelisib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A inducers decrease duvelisib's area under the curve (AUC), potentially reducing its efficacy. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces elacestrant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz reduces eletriptan levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz and elivaldogene autotemcel interact, potentially reducing each other's effects. Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Efavirenz increases eltrombopag levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz reduces elvitegravir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A inducers, as this may lead to decreased plasma concentrations and therapeutic failure. Efavirenz reduces encorafenib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces entrectinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces enzalutamide levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Enzalutamide also reduces efavirenz levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces erdafitinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism but increases its levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and adjust erdafitinib dosage accordingly. Efavirenz increases ergoloid mesylates levels by decreasing their metabolism. This interaction may lead to vasospasm and ischemia. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces ergotamine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism but also increases ergotamine levels by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction may lead to vasospasm and ischemia. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and eribulin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces erythromycin base levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces erythromycin lactobionate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces erythromycin stearate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces ethinylestradiol levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use nonhormonal contraceptives instead. Efavirenz increases ethosuximide levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz increases etrasimod levels or effects. Increased exposure is expected in CYP2C9 poor metabolizers when coadministered with moderate to strong CYP2C8 inhibitors. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz increases etravirine levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz reduces everolimus levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Efavirenz reduces fedratinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The effect of coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers has not been studied. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz increases fexinidazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces finerenone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz and fingolimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz increases fosphenytoin levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz reduces fostamatinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Efavirenz reduces fruquintinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, continue fruquintinib at the recommended dosage. Efavirenz reduces ganaxolone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose but do not exceed the maximum daily dose. Efavirenz and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. Efavirenz reduces glasdegib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. Efavirenz reduces glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with efavirenz may significantly decrease plasma concentrations and AUC, leading to therapeutic failure. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces ibrutinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A inducers decrease ibrutinib plasma concentrations by approximately tenfold. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces idelalisib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease idelalisib systemic exposure. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces indinavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces infigratinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces irinotecan levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces irinotecan liposomal levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces istradefylline levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Itraconazole increases efavirenz levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz reduces itraconazole levels or effects by the same mechanism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces ivabradine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Efavirenz reduces ivacaftor levels by inducing CYP enzymes, while ivacaftor increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces ivosidenib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces ixazomib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A inducers decrease ixazomib Cmax by 54% and AUC by 74%. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Efavirenz reduces larotrectinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, double the larotrectinib dose.
